newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips quiet, SAX index dips 2.08 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips quiet, SAX index dips 2.08 pts.

text.p: Major Slovak shares were mostly quiet in listless trade on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, but losses to share of VUB Bank pulled the 12-share SAX index down 2.08 points to 184.83.
VUB bank lost 15 crowns to close at 1,635, but traded only six shares, which, brokers said, could not show any trend.
Brokers said market continued to lack liquidity, as investors still waited for further decline and stock-holders were reluctant to sell their holdings for offered lower prices.

"Investors active on our market are aware of the fact that there is only a few of them (investors) here, so they seem to be waiting on further decline to buy cheaper, as there is no one else to buy the stocks," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Sykora said that this was behind expectation of a further market's delicline in the near future.
Steel producer VSZ led today's trading, matching 1,905 shares, but closed unchanged at 654 crowns.
Brokers said the share appeared to be overvalued, as most of the demand was at some 640 crowns levels, and added that they expected fall in its price soon.
Refiner Slovnaft and oil and gas storage company Nafta did not trade at all today.
Overall volume fell to 432,469 shares, mainly in direct trades, from 516,105 stocks traded on Wednesday. Turnover decreased to 181.75 million crowns, from 186.1 million.
